title: Bucking contests: Kid Ory against Jack Carey
summary: He tells how Ory and Carey bucked each other with their bands on the wagons.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You remember any, uh, what they call battles of music sometime when you'd run into another? Oh yeah, yeah, yeah.

You'd call that bucking. Bucking. Yeah, yeah, you'd call that bucking. We'd run, there's Kid Oren them, oh, Kid Oren and Jack Carey used to buck all the time. They was known for that, those two, you know. They really used to pick on each other. Both played trombone, you know, and they both had their own band. And they always, one would try to outdo the other one. That was, uh, that was Jack Carey and Kid Oren. When you hear that they was going to advertise Jack Carey and Kid Oren, boy that was a lot of fun there. And everybody was in the streets running behind those wagons to see that, see that bucking. Kid Oren and, uh, and, uh, and Jack Carey. Kid Oren and Jack Carey today is going to play. Kid Oren would, uh, when they'd see if they'd meet them, go around and listen for them. And they'd hear them, you know, and then they'd make their round and go right and meet each other, you know. And then they would stop on the corner. And they'd play a number. And then Jack Carey, he'd play a number. And then Oren, he'd play another number. That's right. See, see, they'd give him a dance, you know, and they was trying to, you know, swing the people to come to hear the real stuff and one was trying to outdo the other one, you know, and both of them was good. You just didn't know what was what. Because both was very good. Yeah.
